headline: How we optimized our LLM pipeline to cut token usage by 70%
summary: Instead of downgrading models, optimizing the entire LLM pipeline led to a 70% reduction in token usage and API spend, while maintaining response quality.
details: Many teams assume switching to a smaller LLM is the fastest way to reduce AI costs, but this often compromises answer quality. Our team found that optimizing the entire pipeline yielded a significant 70% reduction in token usage and API spend without sacrificing response quality.

One major cost driver was using expensive models for simple tasks like summarizing or formatting. Introducing a lightweight routing layer before the LLM, with a simple classifier, directs these requests to more appropriate, cheaper models, dramatically cutting API costs.

Prompts tend to grow over time with new features, often becoming larger than the user's actual question. Periodically reviewing and removing unnecessary instructions keeps prompts concise, consumes fewer tokens, and often maintains or improves response quality.

Traditional caching is ineffective for LLM applications due to varied phrasing (e.g., "How do I request my password?" vs. "I forgot my password"). Semantic caching compares the meaning of requests, returning cached responses for similar queries and significantly reducing duplicate LLM calls.

Sending too much context to an LLM can increase token usage, latency, and cost, sometimes even degrading answer quality. A strategy of retrieving broadly then filtering aggressively ensures the model receives fewer, but significantly more relevant, tokens.

Accidentally asking the model to generate more text than needed, such as explaining its reasoning when only structured data is required, wastes tokens. Directly requesting structured data for specific needs (e.g., destination, dates, budget) optimizes token usage and efficiency.

The biggest cost savings came from reducing unnecessary tokens, intelligently routing requests, caching repeated queries, and providing only essential context. These architectural improvements are crucial as LLM applications move from prototypes to production.

Optimizing an LLM application is about designing a smarter pipeline around the model, rather than just choosing the right model. Measuring token usage is key to identifying the biggest opportunities for improvement outside the model itself.

headline: Gisia: New open-source, self-hosted Git + DevOps tool for personal & small teams
summary: Gisia offers a lightweight, self-hosted platform for Git repos, pipelines, and issue tracking. It runs from a single Docker image, making setup and upgrades simple for small teams.
details: Gisia is a newly unveiled open-source DevOps tool designed for personal and small-team use. It provides a lightweight, self-hosted platform for managing Git repositories, running CI/CD pipelines, and tracking issues, aiming to replace heavier setups.

The entire platform operates from a single Docker image, simplifying deployment significantly. Users can get started with a simple docker compose up command, and upgrades are handled by merely updating the image tag.

Currently in active development, Gisia's creator encourages community feedback to help shape its evolution. The project's source code is available on GitHub for those interested in exploring or contributing.
caption:
